app.title: PathogenWatch BD: influenza surveillance (WHO FluNet)
app.summary: A person picks a country or area and a range of years, and the interface cleans and aggregates the surveillance file into one weekly series. An overview shows the latest complete week, weekly positivity with a confidence band over the number of specimens tested, and an annual table. Further tabs split the series into trend, seasonal and residual parts and test for seasonality. Others mark the weeks that the chosen aberration detectors flag, with a threshold the person can adjust and alert counts for the period. The last tabs compare detector and forecast performance against simple baselines and show the data-quality audit behind the series.

task.text: Screen a weekly surveillance series for its seasonal pattern and for unusual weeks, and check how well detectors and forecasts do against simple baselines.

data.text: Weekly aggregated laboratory surveillance counts per country: specimens processed, positives by type, and the source they were reported under. These are reduced to one positivity series per country with flagged gaps and a provisional last week.
data.item: a country-week of tested specimens and positive detections

stage.text: analysing a cleaned weekly surveillance series for seasonality and aberrations, after auditing the source

mechanism.text: A sidebar country selector and year-range slider drive every tab. Each tab recomputes one analysis on the selected series (positivity with a CI band, STL decomposition, detector alerts overlaid as markers, a forecast versus baselines) and shows it as linked charts and tables. On the detector tab, a multiselect and an optional threshold slider re-score the alerts live.

field.text: prospective aberration detection and seasonality analysis on weekly test-positivity series in infectious disease epidemiology

workflow.name: screen a weekly series for unusual periods against its seasonal baseline

steps.here: The raw surveillance file is de-duplicated, missing totals are recovered from subtype sums, and rows are collapsed to one row per country-week under a source policy. The person then picks a country or area from the sidebar.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: A range slider in the sidebar limits the years shown in the charts and alert counts.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Metric cards show the latest complete week, its positivity, the specimens processed and the count of gap weeks. Below them sit weekly positivity with a 95% band over a bar chart of specimens, and an annual table with type shares.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The series is split into trend, seasonal and residual panels. A harmonic GLM is tested against a null model, a Kruskal-Wallis test compares calendar months, and a table lists each year's peak week.

steps.step: flag the unusual items with a chosen rule
steps.here: The person picks C1/C2/C3/CUSUM detectors and can re-score EARS with a custom z threshold. Alert weeks appear as diamonds on the positivity line, with alert counts for the period.
Detector performance is shown against proxy episodes and a simulation. A one-week-ahead Random Forest is compared with a last-week baseline on a chronological holdout, with MAE, RMSE and R².
The generated data-quality report lists the duplicates removed, the source policy, missingness and consistency checks.

distinctive: Positivity is always shown with its denominator, and weeks with no specimens tested are left undefined rather than set to zero.
The most recent week is treated as provisional and is never alerted on. Weeks with too few specimens are not scored.
Detectors are prospective, using only past data. CUSUM runs on residuals from a seasonal model refit on history and needs three years of history.
With no labelled outbreaks, detection performance is judged against proxy episodes and injected simulated outbreaks, and labelled as such.
Complex forecasts are always benchmarked against a naive last-week baseline on a chronological split.
